title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls
tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

faults.what: The output displays the reply “Right here, Vega.”, but the supplied speech transcription contains only “Rook, you with me?”. Preservation and intelligibility of the reply are therefore not established.

judge.summary: The seven-second output includes the key radio line, but the reply is not confirmed audible and the requested music mix cannot be assessed from the supplied evidence.

must_haves.item: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
must_haves.why: The output is seven seconds and includes the cockpit view shown in the source frame, but one source still cannot establish whether every shot and subtitle is unchanged.

must_haves.item: A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
must_haves.why: Neither the images nor the speech transcription establishes the presence, mood, or instrumentation of music.

must_haves.item: The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
must_haves.why: The key line is explicitly reported as heard, but the visibly subtitled reply is not included in the transcription; preservation of all calls and their synchronization cannot be confirmed.

must_haves.item: During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
must_haves.why: The reported peak of -1.7 dB does not establish relative voice and music levels or masking during individual lines.

must_haves.item: The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.
must_haves.why: No supplied audio description confirms audible music or its level relative to speech.
